description:
Price the session cart, returning each line's offers (price + days).

Prices every line that changed since its last quote; pass a `line_id` to
re-price just one. Each line's translated configuration + offers are
snapshotted so the payment link re-sends the priced line and binds an offer
by `offer_id`. A line with a `pricing_error` was refused by RendReal: on
`invalid_configuration` re-run `catalog_configure_product` for that
`line_id` using the reason, then quote again; on `unparseable_response`
RendReal's response was unusable — retry later. The other lines still
priced. A line with an empty `offers` list and no `pricing_error` didn't
price — relay that, don't treat it as an error. Returns offers for the
whole cart.
List the offers in your reply as short plain text, never as a markdown
table. When the quote card is displayed, it shows each offer with a
"Choose this" button, so a short summary is enough.

The widget's picker commits an ordinal reference with price and
production days attached for disambiguation (e.g. "Nr 2 - £58.00
(3-day production), please.") rather than an id — 1-indexed against
that same line's `offers` list from this call, in order. Map the
number back to that list position's `offer_id`; don't match on price
or production days alone (two offers can coincide on either).

Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED. On failure the job error is
`EmptyCartError` (nothing configured yet), `LineNotFoundError` (bad
`line_id`), `ProductNotFoundError` (catalog entry gone),
`RendrealNotConfiguredError`, a `ConfigurationMismatchError` /
`UnmappableComponentError`, or a `Rendreal*Error`.
name: order_get_quote

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).
